name: Schwoich
kurzbeschreibung: Charming residential community in the Inntal valley, boasting a picturesque location by Walchsee and the gardens of the Kaisergebirge.
beschreibung:
Overview

Schwoich is situated at 583 meters above sea level on a sunny plateau in the Tyrolean Lower Inn Valley, just south of the fortress town of Kufstein beneath the crags of Mount Scheffauer (2,111 m, Wilder Kaiser). With approximately 2,600 residents, the municipality is traditionally structured as an ensemble of dispersed historical hamlets known as Banndörfl, including Osterndorf, Sonnendorf, Amberg, and Egerbach. Schwoich uniquely combines traditional Tyrolean farming heritage with monumental industrial history: as the birthplace of the Austrian cement industry, it played a pioneer role in European construction. Today, the village thrives as a welcoming, forward-looking destination featuring Tyrol's first ecological swimming lake, an award-winning craft brewery, and scenic hiking trails overlooking the Kaiser mountains.

History

Settled during Bavarian migrations in the 6th century, Schwoich was first documented in 1280 under the name Swiuch, originating from an Old High German word denoting marshy ground. The community gained industrial prominence in 1841/1842 when master road builder Franz Kink discovered hydraulic marl deposits in the Glemmtal valley and established the Austrian Empire’s very first Roman cement factory. Industrialist Angelo Saullich later expanded Portland cement production, paving the way for the Perlmooser cement corporation. Due to the smoke-spewing kilns operating around the clock, locals affectionately nicknamed the district Russland (Soot-Land). A historic shaft kiln is proudly depicted on the municipal coat of arms. The parish church of Saint Giles, first recorded in 1390, received an acclaimed modern expansion in 1974/1975 designed by renowned Austrian architect Clemens Holzmeister.

Getting there

Schwoich enjoys prime transport accessibility. By car, exit the A12 Inntal motorway at Kufstein Süd (toll-free when arriving from Germany via Kiefersfelden) and take the B173 Eiberg road towards Söll, turning right after three kilometers onto the Schwoich plateau. By train, arrive at the international rail hubs in Kufstein or Wörgl. VVT bus line 4026 operates hourly connecting Kufstein railway station with Schwoich, Bad Häring, and Wörgl. Overnight visitors travel free of charge on local public buses with the KufsteinerlandCard.

Tips

Discover European industrial heritage at the open-air Schwoich Cement Museum in the Russland district, featuring original 1842 shaft kilns and interpretive walking paths. On warm days, cool off at the Bananensee, Tyrol’s first natural ecological swimming pond, filtered entirely without chemicals and equipped with sunbathing lawns and a Kneipp pool. Beer enthusiasts should visit the pioneering Bierol craft brewery at the historic Stöfflhof farm, home to award-winning IPAs and the acclaimed Zur Linä taproom restaurant. Scenic hiking routes lead across the Steinerne Stiege path to the alpine pastures of Walleralm and the shores of Lake Hintersteiner See.
